name: Multiple Sclerosis Variant

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Revised McDonald Criteria (adapted for variant forms)

criteria.description: Evidence of lesions disseminated in space on MRI or clinical examination
Evidence of lesions disseminated in time demonstrated by MRI or clinical relapse
Presence of oligoclonal bands in cerebrospinal fluid supportive of diagnosis
Exclusion of alternative diagnoses through clinical, laboratory, and imaging studies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Dissemination in space and time demonstrated by clinical or MRI findings plus exclusion of alternative diagnoses; supportive CSF findings enhance diagnostic confidence
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnostic criteria adapted to account for atypical presentations and variant clinical courses

searchTerms: brain MRI showing finger-like white matter lesions
specific brain lesions seen on MRI scans
characteristic MRI spots in brain white matter

pathognomonic.symptomName: Optic neuritis with unilateral visual loss
searchTerms: inflammation of optic nerve causing vision loss
optic nerve swelling with visual impairment

common.symptomName: Lhermitte’s sign (electric shock sensation on neck flexion)
searchTerms: electric shock feeling when bending neck
tingling or shock sensation on neck flexion
abnormal skin feelings like pins and needles
sudden need to urinate and leaking urine
loss of bladder control and frequent urination

laboratory: Presence of oligoclonal bands in cerebrospinal fluid
imaging: MRI showing periventricular, juxtacortical, infratentorial, and spinal cord lesions
genetic: No specific causative gene identified; HLA-DRB1*15:01 allele associated with increased susceptibility
other: Evoked potentials showing delayed conduction in central nervous system pathways

distinguishingFeatures: Diffuse, large demyelinating lesions on MRI

redFlags: Poor response to standard MS therapies
Presence of systemic symptoms suggesting alternative diagnosis
references: Thompson AJ, et al. Diagnosis of multiple sclerosis: 2017 revisions of the McDonald criteria. Lancet Neurol. 2018.
Wingerchuk DM, et al. International consensus diagnostic criteria for neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorders. Neurology. 2015.
Compston A, Coles A. Multiple sclerosis. Lancet. 2008.
